# Clean room and licences

pysacd was built so that nobody has to worry about where its code came from.

## No Philips/ISO reference code, anywhere

The MPEG-4 reference DST decoder isn't GPL-compatible. That includes code
derived from it, such as sacd-ripper's `libdstdec`. It has never been in this
repository, its history, its issues or its CI, and contributors may not read
it (see [CLAUDE.md](../CLAUDE.md)).

## The SACD engine: scarletbook-rs

Since 0.3.0 pysacd reads disc images with [scarletbook-rs](https://github.com/aclater/scarletbook-rs)
(#85): the sector layout, the master and area TOCs, the audio sectors and DST decoding. It is
a Rust library written in a clean room of its own, only from the specifications and
conformance corpus of [sacd-spec](https://github.com/aclater/sacd-spec); its clean-room record is
its `CLEANROOM.md`.

- pysacd uses it as a released, signed binary through its C interface (see
  [development](development.md#the-scarletbook-library)).
- Nothing of pysacd's goes into it, and nothing from it is copied into pysacd.
- Requirements pysacd finds are filed with scarletbook-rs as issues, never as patches.

pysacd's own code is what turns the audio into files: the DSF, DSDIFF, WAV and FLAC writers,
DSD-to-PCM conversion, `sacd_extract`-compatible naming, cue sheets, XML and `-P` text,
tagging and MusicBrainz, and the PS3 client.

## Up to 0.2: pysacd's own DST decoder

Up to 0.2.2, pysacd had its own TOC parser, sector demultiplexer and DST decoder. The decoder
started from FFmpeg's DST decoder by Peter Ross (LGPL-2.1+), and FFmpeg's missing parts
(segmentation, general mapping, the full validity checks) were added through a two-agent
clean room. One agent studied the reference and wrote a prose specification, with no code;
a second agent, which never saw the reference, implemented from that document alone.

All of that left the repository with #85; it is in its history.
- The specification:
  [`docs/dst-bitstream.md` at v0.2.2](https://github.com/aclater/pysacd/blob/v0.2.2/docs/dst-bitstream.md).
- The decoder: `csrc/dstdec.c` at the same tag.

The test-only DST encoder that builds pysacd's synthetic DST discs (`tests/native/dstenc.c`,
`tests/dstenc.py`) was written from that specification and stays, as a test fixture.

## sacd_extract only as a black box

`sacd_extract` is used as a compiled oracle to compare output against,
locally and in CI, where it is built from a pinned upstream commit. Its source
is never copied or paraphrased into this repository. Where pysacd matches its
behaviour (file names, DSDIFF layout, `-P` text), the behaviour was
established by running the binary and comparing output.

## Licences

| Part | Licence |
|---|---|
| pysacd as a whole | GPL-2.0-or-later |
| [scarletbook-rs](https://github.com/aclater/scarletbook-rs), linked into the engine | MIT OR Apache-2.0, used under MIT |
| the Rust standard library and crates inside it (rayon, crossbeam, either, thiserror) | MIT OR Apache-2.0, used under MIT |
| libFLAC (optional, for FLAC output) | BSD-3-Clause |
| mutagen (optional, for tagging) | GPL-2.0-or-later |

New code is GPL-2.0-or-later, and since 0.3.0 all of pysacd is. `csrc/compat.h`, which was
LGPL-2.1-or-later so that the FFmpeg-derived decoder could include it, is GPL-2.0-or-later now
that the decoder is gone. No dependency or copied code under incompatible terms may be added.
pysacd takes scarletbook-rs and its Rust dependencies under MIT, since Apache-2.0 isn't
compatible with GPL-2.0; their notices are in `licenses/` and in every wheel.

## Acknowledgements

- **[scarletbook-rs](https://github.com/aclater/scarletbook-rs)** and
  **[sacd-spec](https://github.com/aclater/sacd-spec)**: the engine since 0.3.0, and the
  specification and corpus it was written from.
- **[sacd-ripper](https://github.com/sacd-ripper/sacd-ripper)**: the
  Scarletbook layouts and `sacd_extract`'s behaviour, which pysacd reproduces.
  Its compiled binary was the oracle throughout.
- **FFmpeg's DST decoder** by Peter Ross (LGPL-2.1+), the base of pysacd's DST decoder up to
  0.2.
- **Sebastian Gesemann's dsd2pcm** (BSD-3-Clause), credited for the technique
  in `csrc/dsp.c`'s first DSD-to-PCM stage: lookup tables of filter partial
  sums indexed by whole DSD bytes.
- **[MusicBrainz](https://musicbrainz.org)** and the **Cover Art Archive**,
  for tags and covers.
- The **PS3 SACD Ripper** homebrew, whose protocol pysacd speaks.
